nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 3b — 3MF Ingest
nodes.rationale: Split out of slice 3 so that adding the workspace's first ZIP and first XML dependency gets a review of its own rather than riding along with geometry work. Writes no SQL at all.

nodes.label: parse_3mf
nodes.rationale: Reads the OPC package with zip, follows _rels/.rels to the model part, and streams its XML with quick-xml, merging every build item's transformed mesh into the one Mesh the rest of the pipeline already handles. One file rather than four, because splitting .rels resolution from the mesh parse would put two halves of one decision in two files.

nodes.label: Caps
nodes.rationale: Zip-bomb defence: decompressed size, entry count, ratio and path traversal, applied as bytes arrive rather than after. Each breach must name which bound fired — sharing one error message across two bounds is how the absolute size cap went untested behind the ratio cap.

nodes.label: read_capped
nodes.rationale: Refuses as bytes arrive, not after. The mutation proving it must use a bounded source that counts bytes pulled: read_to_end on an infinite reader does not hang, it allocates until the OOM killer fires — it took the machine down twice at 10.9 GB and 13.2 GB on a 15 GB host.

nodes.label: Compression
nodes.rationale: SourceStore::put takes a compression policy so an already-compressed container like 3MF is stored as-is. Proven by measurement rather than assertion: the 3MF row saved 0.0% while the OBJ beside it saved 49.6% and the STLs 79.7-92.7%, which is what makes it a policy rather than compression having stopped working.

nodes.label: Build Transforms and Component Recursion
nodes.rationale: A multi-item build plate is one part with its triangles summed and its bbox spanning the placements. Both the transform/scale ordering and the composition order shipped correct and unpinned: a translation in a millimetre file has scale 1, a pure scale matrix commutes with a scalar, and identity 3x3 blocks make a transposed product give the same answer — so both orderings passed every test.

nodes.label: Dependency Audit as Its Own Slice
nodes.rationale: cargo-deny was not installed on the machine, and auditing the two new dependencies is the slice's whole premise — so task 1 installs it and runs it for real rather than deferring to CI. Two dependencies, both named in the spec, and no others: if a task feels like it needs a third, it is the wrong task.
